notes: Event date: Hitler relieved Geyr two days after he relieved Rundstedt on 2 July, that is on 4 July (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 2 p. 28); Eberbach was about to relieve Geyr at the beginning of July (ch. 3 p. 47); Wikipedia's Eberbach page says he took command on 4 July, two days after Geyr was relieved. Wikipedia's Fifth Panzer Army page gives 2 July for the relief and the replacement (G019 alternate). Event support: the event itself is stated in the cited text (see Event date); only the headquarters place is a representative point. Location support fallback: no source read gives the headquarters place for 4 July; the point is Thury-Harcourt, the approximate headquarters of claim C0187 (28 June), used as a representative point.
